Siora is an Earth Observation and AI company developing satellite-based soil and crop intelligence solutions for agriculture.
Our core soil intelligence solution provides field-level estimates of parameters including nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), pH, soil organic matter, cation exchange capacity (CEC), soil texture and other physical soil properties. The resulting spatial maps can be used to identify variability within fields, support fertilisation planning, create management zones and enable variable-rate applications.

Our technology transforms satellite imagery and other geospatial data into actionable information about agricultural fields. By combining Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 observations with terrain, climate, geological and other environmental data, together with machine learning models, Siora can estimate key soil characteristics at high spatial resolution without requiring extensive physical soil sampling.
In addition to soil analysis, Siora develops Earth Observation tools for continuous agricultural monitoring, including vegetation condition, water stress and moisture-related indicators. Our objective is to turn complex remote sensing data into information that farmers, agronomists and agricultural companies can use directly in operational decision-making.
The platform is designed to provide analysis rapidly and at scale, from individual agricultural fields to large farming portfolios. Results can be delivered through Siora's web platform as well as through standard geospatial and data formats for integration into other farm management and precision agriculture systems.
Siora is particularly interested in collaboration and R&D projects involving Earth Observation, precision agriculture, soil monitoring and mapping, sustainable fertilisation, variable-rate application, crop and vegetation monitoring, water stress, climate-smart agriculture, land management and the development of new downstream applications of satellite data.
We are open to participating in ESA and European collaborative projects as a technology provider, Earth Observation data analytics partner, AI/ML partner, agricultural use-case provider or pilot and validation partner.

entityDescription:
AquaGuard Technologies AB (AGT) is a Swedish dual use deep tech company developing NEXUS, its proprietary AI enabled operational intelligence platform for Civil, Security and Defence applications. With a primary specialisation in the maritime domain, AGT addresses the technically challenging detection, classification, monitoring, tracking and identification of small and non cooperative vessels, including vessels operating without AIS, MMSI or other RF based identification. NEXUS combines AGT's proprietary software, AI/ML models, algorithms, processing pipelines, Multi Source Fusion and Correlation, Decision Intelligence, system architecture and operational workflows to transform fragmented observations into decision ready operational intelligence.
AGT has developed and validated AI/ML capability for precise small vessel detection and classification from high resolution satellite data, generating confidence, geolocation and associated object information independently of cooperative vessel transmissions. High resolution Optical and SAR provide complementary sensing capabilities, enabling observations from different acquisition times and conditions to be correlated within NEXUS. This extends vessel detection, classification and monitoring beyond the limitations of individual sensors and conventional cooperative tracking systems.
NEXUS brings together three complementary intelligence pillars: Space Data from high resolution Optical and SAR sources; Ground Edge AI from UAVs, USVs, fixed sensors and other local assets; and Ancillary and Contextual Data including AIS, historical records, weather, OSINT, infrastructure and partner data. Multi Source Fusion and Correlation associates these observations through entity resolution, spatial and temporal correlation, track association, confidence fusion and contextual enrichment. Decision Intelligence converts the resulting operational picture into confidence and risk assessments, anomaly and pattern analysis, operational alerts and decision support.
The same architecture supports persistent object association and cross modal vessel Re Identification (ReID), allowing observations across different times, locations and sensing modalities to contribute to an evolving digital identity and history for each vessel. Where AIS, MMSI or other identifying information is available, it can be correlated with that identity; where conventional identifiers are absent, NEXUS can maintain the observed vessel intelligence independently. This creates a pathway for persistent monitoring and identification of small and non cooperative vessels across multiple observations and sensing sources.
NEXUS is modular, sensor agnostic and interoperable, enabling additional sensors, data sources, AI models and intelligence functions to be incorporated within the same operational environment. Secure dashboards, APIs and structured geospatial outputs support direct use of NEXUS intelligence and integration with existing operational, GIS and command environments. The platform is designed to deliver timely intelligence to operational and regulatory users, with near real time capability where source acquisition and data availability permit.
NEXUS supports Civil applications including maritime safety, environmental monitoring and compliance, critical infrastructure, energy and emergency response; Security applications including maritime, border, coastal and critical infrastructure security; and Defence applications including ISR, maritime domain awareness, force protection and defence asset monitoring. The current NEXUS beta platform is deployed on AWS at TRL 6 and is progressing toward TRL 7 through continued system integration and representative operational validation.

Taranis develops a dedicated Molniya‑orbit constellation that delivers persistent polar coverage and merges optical/IR imaging with communications relay. By integrating connectivity, data and transport into a single system, we bring fiber‑like service to the world’s most underserved regions.

REDAR is a Greek deep-tech company developing lightweight optical sensing payloads for unmanned aerial vehicles, bringing space-grade measurement technology to terrestrial applications. Engineered as a compact payload for integration on standard UAV platforms, it enables mobile, source-level emissions monitoring that fixed and handheld methods cannot provide.

The system is built around a single modular optical core: by reconfiguring the sensing module, the same platform extends across environmental monitoring, industrial safety and defence, allowing one engineering effort to serve multiple civil and dual-use markets. Incubated at ESA BIC Greece, REDAR has a working demonstrator validated in both laboratory and field conditions and is now advancing toward a flight-ready instrument.

StormGeo is a global provider of advanced weather intelligence and decision-support solutions for shipping, energy and weather-sensitive industries. Founded in Bergen, Norway, in 1998 and part of Alfa Laval, we transform complex environmental data into actionable insights that help organizations improve safety, operational efficiency and resilience.

Our capabilities include the ingestion and fusion of Earth-observation data, satellite and radar imagery, meteorological and ocean models, in-situ observations and customer asset data. We apply remote sensing, geospatial analytics, AI and machine learning to deliver site-specific forecasts, hazard monitoring, maritime and offshore decision support, energy-market intelligence, and infrastructure-risk services. Solutions are delivered through scalable cloud platforms, APIs, operational dashboards and automated alerts, supported by meteorologists and domain experts operating 24/7/365.

StormGeo processes more than 15 TB of data per day and delivers over 10 million forecasts annually across approximately 68,000 locations. Our services support thousands of offshore sites and vessels worldwide.

StormGeo was the prime contractor for GridEyeS, an ESA Business Applications project integrating Copernicus Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data, commercial high-resolution imagery, AI-based analytics and meteorological intelligence. GridEyeS demonstrated scalable vegetation monitoring, change detection, infrastructure-risk assessment and emergency-response support for electricity transmission and distribution networks. The service was validated with grid operators and developed into a commercially available operational solution.

We welcome collaboration with satellite and Earth-observation data providers, geospatial and AI technology partners, research organizations, infrastructure operators and downstream service providers. We are particularly interested in partnerships that turn space-derived data into scalable operational services for energy, maritime operations, critical infrastructure and climate resilience.
